content:
Maya Patel: heads up — noticed high tail latency on hosted API, us-west GPU pool ~95% for last 20m. queue_depth metric jumped and we started 429'ing some keys. thinking we need capacity-aware admission not just static token buckets.
Aj Chen: ugh saw that alert. which keys are hitting 429s? orgs or individual API keys? :grimacing:
Maya Patel: mostly mid-tier orgs, a couple of runaway API keys during a batch job. it's causing backpressure that cascades into longer kv-cache wait times.
Kevin O'Neill: agree — static per-key token-bucket is brittle. proposal: compute per-region capacity units from available GPUs and map that onto a dynamic refill rate for org buckets.
Lucy Morales: +1. we should include queue_length and gpu_util in the refill formula so refill_rate drops as saturation grows. naive formula:
```
refill_rate = base_rate * max(0.1, 1 - alpha*gpu_util - beta*(queue_depth / qcap))
```
where gpu_util in [0,1], qcap is expected safe queue depth.
Raj Singh: question: do we keep per-key hard caps (absolute tokens) + org-level soft pool? or fully pooled?
Aj Chen: I think hybrid: per-key soft token bucket that can borrow from org pool when headroom exists, but org pool shrinks when region headroom low. means a noisy key can't starve others when capacity tight.
Maya Patel: exactly. and fallback policy when borrow fails: degrade model size (gpt-medium -> gpt-small) or switch to cached responses for repeats.
ops-bot: alert: GPU util us-west-1 > 90% for 22m, queue_depth > 1200, 432 requests 429'd in last 5m.
Kevin O'Neill: operational concerns: we need to ensure refill calc is stable and not oscillatory. suggest exponential smoothing on gpu_util and queue_depth samples (window ~30s) before computing refill_rate. also add min_refill to avoid starving health-check traffic.
Lucy Morales: implementation sketch in admission controller (pseudocode):
```
metrics = sample_metrics(region)
util = ema(metrics.gpu_util, 30s)
q = ema(metrics.queue_depth, 30s)
org_headroom = region_capacity_units - committed_usage
org_refill = clamp(base_org_rate * (org_headroom / region_capacity_units), min_org, max_org)
per_key_refill = base_key_rate * (org_refill / total_org_keys)
```
Raj Singh: how do we surface this in billing/quotas? if refill fluctuates, customers will see variable throughput. need clear doc and maybe SLA tiers: guaranteed commit (dedicated) vs best-effort (hosted).
Aj Chen: yep tie to product tiers. hosted gets best-effort capacity-aware rates with throttle windows. dedicated customers get fixed capacity units.
Maya Patel: testing plan: simulate noisy keys + gradual GPU saturation in staging. run chaos job that injects heavy prefix requests and ensure borrow/stealing logic prevents global meltdown.
Kevin O'Neill: also add safety net: if overall region util > 97% then reject new requests proactively with 503 + Retry-After to avoid OOM or model crash.
Lucy Morales: small note on metrics: expose token_bucket_refill_rate, org_pool_remaining_tokens, region_capacity_units to console + alerts so SRE can see when borrow is happening.
Aj Chen: one more edge case — cross-region routing. if us-west tight, we can route non-data-residency requests to eu-west if headroom exists. need routing policy in admission controller.
Maya Patel: agreed. i'll draft a short design doc with formula options, smoothing params, and an integration test plan. will ping for reviews. :thumbsup:
Raj Singh: ack, please include failure-mode diagrams (what happens when controller restarts and pool states lost).
Kevin O'Neill: +1, and add a canary rollout for 1% traffic first.
ops-bot: note: created incident ticket INF-4821 for the us-west saturation event.
Maya Patel: thanks all — target PR early next week.
